summary.text: Harry Bhandari is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 8 who has served since January 2019 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Born in Nepal, he is an educator who holds a Ph.D. from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, and he sits on the House Economic Matters Committee.

paragraphs.text: Bhandari was born in Nepal on October 1, 1977, and immigrated to the United States in 2005.

His legislative biography lists graduate study in educational leadership and administration at The Johns Hopkins University and a Ph.D. in literacy and culture from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, in 2022.
He worked as an English teacher, author, principal and lecturer in Kathmandu, Nepal, and later as a teacher in Baltimore City Schools and adjunct faculty at Baltimore City Community College.
Ballotpedia also lists work as a gas station attendant.
Bhandari was first elected to the House in 2018 and has served since January 9, 2019.
He served on the Health and Government Operations Committee from 2019 to 2025 and now sits on the Economic Matters Committee, where he chairs the Land Use and Zoning Subcommittee.
He has chaired the Maryland Legislative Asian-American and Pacific Islander Caucus and has served on the Baltimore County Pedestrian and Bicycle Advisory Committee since 2013.
In 2024 he ran in the Democratic primary for Maryland's 2nd Congressional District, finishing second with 8.5 percent of the vote behind John Olszewski Jr.
He advanced from the Democratic primary for District 8 on June 23, 2026.
